Open • FLYBYME (Tim) opened about 24 minutes ago • 0 comments
Labels: package


  The fleet works and cannot yet be operated. Three things, batched.          
                                                                              
  --------                                                                    
                                                                              
  ## 1. Groups, stored as a reference — not expanded at assign time           
                                                                              
   NodeSchema  is  { hostname, services[] } . Assigning seven machines one    
  service                                                                     
  at a time is not how anyone will use it. A group is a named set —  serve ,  
   edge ,  build  — and a node holds groups and individual services, so an    
  exception does not force a new group.                                       
                                                                              
  The decision, taken: store the reference and let it roll. Adding a service  
  to                                                                          
   serve  starts it on every node in that group. The alternative — expanding  
  the                                                                         
  group at assign time and freezing the result — means every group edit needs 
  a                                                                           
  manual re-assign of every node, which is exactly the failure that leaves    
   demos.localhost  serving a chrome from two days ago.                       
                                                                              
  This is the same fork as compose-vs-rolling for releases, in a second place,
  and                                                                         
  it gets the same answer. Say in your plan how a group edit reaches a        
  connected                                                                   
  node, and what happens to a node that is offline when the group changes.    
                                                                              
  Starting groups:  serve  =  api  +  identity  +  fleet  +  catalog ;        
   edge  =  cdn ;  build  =  builder .                                        
                                                                              
  ## 2.  node.provision  — a separate verb from  node.assign                  
                                                                              
  "it would be nice to have git clone/pull and npm i/update so I can remote   
  load                                                                        
  any number of services."                                                    
                                                                              
  This needs no new loading mechanism. The Supervisor's manifest entry is     
   { name, path, dependsOn, mountKey }  where  path  is "where to dynamically 
   import()  the compiled service module from — resolved relative to the      
  manifest                                                                    
  file's own directory if not absolute." Absolute paths already work. A node  
  that                                                                        
  clones a repo and installs it has a valid manifest entry pointing into it.  
                                                                              
  Keep the two verbs apart and the model stays clean:                         
                                                                              
  •  node.assign  is a switch. Unchanged. Which of the available services run.
  •  node.provision  makes new switches exist. Clone or pull, install,        
  register a manifest entry.                                                  
                                                                              
  Collapsing them makes "what can this node run" and "what is it running" one 
  confused thing, and  node.status  stops meaning anything.                   
                                                                              
  Two requirements that are not negotiable:                                   
                                                                              
  • A ref, not a branch. A pinned commit or tag. A node that pulls  main      
  changes behaviour when somebody else pushes — the mutable-version problem   
  wearing a different hat, and the catalog already refuses that.              
  •  npm i  runs arbitrary install scripts. Provisioning is therefore a       
  remote code execution primitive on every machine we own.  operator  gate,   
  and an allowlist of repositories. This is the sharpest instance of "limit   
  the attack surface" in the system and it must not ship without both.        
                                                                              
  ## 3. Two supervisors, one boundary                                         
                                                                              
  Live deployment is systemd + Atlas.                                         
                                                                              
  • systemd owns the process. It restarts the node if it dies.                
  • the Supervisor owns services inside that process. Start and stop without  
  restarting anything.                                                        
                                                                              
  So  node.assign  must never require a process restart — the current         
  implementation is right and this is a property to keep and to test. If      
  assignment                                                                  
  ever needs a restart, systemd's restart policy and the fleet's desired state
  become two authorities over one thing.                                      
                                                                              
  Atlas: every node points at the same  MONGODB_URI . Nothing to build; note  
  it.                                                                         
                                                                              
  ## 4. Bootstrap is an IP, permanently                                       
                                                                              
  The head is  surf.surfdns.net  at 169.197.131.82, and DNS does not work —   
  it is the product being built. A nameserver platform whose control plane    
  resolves                                                                    
  its own head by name loses the ability to reach the machines that would fix 
  DNS,                                                                        
  precisely when DNS is broken.                                               
                                                                              
  So the bootstrap address is an IP, not as a stopgap but as the design.      
   --bootstrap  /  MESH_BOOTSTRAP  already accept one; write the reason down  
  where                                                                       
  somebody will find it before "improving" it to a hostname.                  
                                                                              
  Worth knowing:  surf  has 981MB of RAM and is the tightest box in the fleet.

    Fleet: groups that roll, reconcile as a verb, and an operator check that checks
    
    Three things, and the first is a hole rather than a feature.
    
    **requireOperator, and an absent caller is not an operator.** The check was
    assertOperatorIfUserPresent: it verified the role only when ctx.meta.user
    happened to be there, and admitted the call outright when it was not. Every
    caller reaching these tools over the broker rather than through the HTTP gate --
    which is every mesh peer -- arrives with no meta.user, so the fleet's control
    surface was open to anything already on the mesh. Roadmap C2.5: no internal
    bypass, no god token, no trusted-caller exemption. Being on the mesh is not an
    identity. Four tests were calling assign and status with no caller and passing.
    
    node.hello is the one exception and its reasoning is written down: a machine has
    no user and never will, so an operator check there means no node can register,
    and the workaround it pushes you toward -- an operator credential on every box --
    hands the whole control surface to every box. What bounds it is that the contract
    is internal so no site can expose it (now pinned by a test), and that a peer only
    reaches the broker by presenting the shared key at the handshake.
    
    **Groups store a reference, not an expansion.** Expanding at assign time and
    keeping the result means every group edit needs a manual re-assign of every node,
    and the nodes nobody remembers go on running yesterday's set -- the same failure
    that leaves a site serving a part from two days ago. A node holds groups and
    services and the desired set is the union, so one machine that also runs a
    builder does not need a group of its own. Both fields are optional and absent
    means unchanged, not empty: putting a node in a group must not silently clear
    what it was given directly.
    
    **node.reconcile is the verb that makes a group mean something.** Editing a group
    changes no running process; reconciling does. Idempotent, so it is safe on a
    timer, by hand, and twice. It does not stop at the first failure -- nine healthy
    nodes still need to converge when the tenth is wedged. Extracted from assign
    because there are now three ways a desired set changes and three copies would be
    three chances to disagree about what a difference is.
    
    Stops before starts: surf has 981MB and starting the new service first can mean
    neither fits.
    
    Refs surfdns#45.
